brief:
A poll shows American sympathy toward Palestine has surpassed sympathy toward Israel for the first time, according to Shehab Wire. The finding reflects a shift in how the American public views the Israeli-Palestinian conflict after decades of polling that typically showed greater U.S. backing for Israel.

The survey data underscores evolving attitudes among Americans on the dispute. Sympathy levels toward each side have fluctuated over time, but this represents the first instance in which Palestinian support has overtaken Israeli support in U.S. public opinion measurements. The reversal comes as the conflict continues to draw international attention and shape debates within American political discourse.
